entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abd-Allah Hatefi, widely known as Hatefi, was a preeminent Persian epic poet of the late Timurid and early Safavid eras, flourishing in the cultural crucible of Khurasan and Transoxiana before his death in 1521. As the nephew and protégé of the celebrated polymath Nur ad-Din Abd ar-Rahman Jami, Hatefi inherited and masterfully adapted the classical tradition of Nizami Ganjavi, solidifying his reputation as a formidable narrative poet whose works were widely read and copied across the Persianate world. His contributions helped bridge the literary styles of the waning Timurid Renaissance and the nascent Safavid artistic patronage, cementing his place in the continuous lineage of Persian epic poetry.

Hatefi's most significant achievement lies in his own rendition of the *Khamsah* (Quintet), a collection of five epic poems mirroring the structure established by Nizami. His *Layli and Majnun* reimagined the timeless Arab love story with profound psychological depth, while his *Shirin andus Khusraw* offered a distinct interpretation of the Sasanian romance. Perhaps his most original work, *Timurnama* (also known as *Zafarnama*), chronicles the conquests of Timur, providing a valuable historical and literary account of the conqueror's campaigns, completed around 1499. These works, composed in the intricate *masnavi* form, showcased his command of prosody and narrative artistry, captivating audiences from Herat to Istanbul.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hatefi's masterful reinterpretation of classical Persian epics and his unique *Timurnama* ensured the continuity and evolution of the *Khamsah* tradition, significantly influencing subsequent literary and artistic production across the Persianate world for centuries.
